lines.t: Easy now. Bowl's warm, troupe's warmer. What can Knellstone's Hearthrest do for you?

options.label: Help a kin recall a move

lines.t: Easy now. Bowl's warm, troupe's warmer. Off you go.
Buy something or admire the dust. Both are free until you touch.
Buy something or admire the dust. Both are free until you touch.
How's the songbook? Every verse you sing, I copy into the master Kinsong. In very small handwriting.
Ten verses sung and I'll have something useful for you. If I'm not here, try Galewick — I follow the migrations.
You're the one from Larkhollow! I'm compiling the Kinsong — every verse in Cantarra.
Show me what you've heard and I'll pay in useful things. Chimes, mostly. Chimes are always useful.
Shh — I'm listening to the tea. Knellstone water hums a quarter-tone flat. I'm writing a paper.
Somebody's making an enormous racket up on the ridge road. If that's your friend, come back when it's over.
Hear the noon peal? Three bells, one chord. I cried a bit. Don't tell the quarry, they think I'm made of granite.
East, Crane and Quarry — all three ringing true! Whatever those ear-muffed folk did to them, it's undone.
Bellwright's fee, paid backwards for once. And a couple of cure-alls — ringing in your ears is a real hazard.
A proper bronze clapper! Hand it here. That goes in the East Bell — hear it? Ding. Correct ding.
Another clapper — lovely weight on it. Into the Crane Bell she goes. Dong. That's a happy dong.
The last clapper! The Quarry Bell's been sulking for a week. There. Bong. Talk to me again, I'm overcome.
Three bells: the East Bell by the Hall steps, the Crane Bell by the quarry, the Quarry Bell out west.
An electric kin can Spark a bell back into tune. Or bring me clappers — the old ones rolled off down Brackenridge.
Sixty years I've tuned Knellstone's bells. Then fellows in brass ear-muffs 'measured' them, and now they're off-key.
Clappers knocked loose, tone gone sour. Would you help an old bellwright set them right?
Hear that? Neither do I. Three bells gone flat as a mill-pond. Somebody's been fiddling.
Hall's shut while Dorran walks the ridge. Once the town's back to its racket, come see me.
The miners came up singing! My Dunn's got his Rollith back, fat as a pudding. You did that, I hear.
Say what you like about those surveyors, they feed a stray well. Still. Nobody asked them to.
Those ear-muffed surveyors packed their tripods and went down the Undertone. With coils. Lots of coils.
The miners' kin started wandering off the same day. I'm not saying it's connected. I'm saying it loudly, though.
There's surveyors in brass ear-muffs measuring the bell towers. Say the stones need *servicing*.
Never knew stone needed servicing. My sister Nell over in Galewick says they're everywhere. She'd know. She knows everything.
You beat Cantor Dorran?! Did he do the face? The face where he's pleased but only his eyebrows know?
See that Rollith? It rolls the quarry spoil downhill for the miners. Then it rolls back up to do it again. Forever. It LOVES it.
And the Cairnback pulls the ore cart. Yesterday the cart won. Nobody's allowed to talk about it.
Listen to her hum! Crane lift's running sweet since you Sparked the lode. Found that Silver Chime up top, then?
Crane lift's lode went flat the day the hum dropped. Brass needs a buzz to turn, see.
A Spark from an electric kin would wake it. Somebody left a Silver Chime on the top platform, if you're curious.
Kett's crew came up with every one of their kin. First smile I've seen on a miner since the hum stopped.
The up-shaft past the lower galleries comes out in Sallowfen. Wet feet guaranteed.
Dorran's Keynote on your belt? Then the chain's off. Down you go — Foreman Kett's camp is just inside.
Miners say their kin have gone wandering below since the hum dropped. If you see a round one called Pebbles, she bites.
Lift's chained, I'm afraid. Knell Hall's orders: Keynote holders only below. The Undertone doesn't forgive beginners.
Win Cantor Dorran's Keynote and I'll let you down myself. With a lantern. I'm not a monster.
Bell tower three is a quarter-tone flat. We'll be servicing it. And the stone under it. Routine.
The Magister says unregulated stones are how people get hurt. She's usually right about hazards.
Licensed survey. Please step back from the equipment.
We don't *take* kin. We collect strays. There's a difference. There's a form for it.
You did it! Did he tell you you'd have made a fair quarryman? He only says that to people he likes.
Cantor Dorran's back from his walk — the Hall's open! I'm going in. Tomorrow. Probably.
Tip: the pillars inside are tuned. Beat a hall Tuner and a row sinks. Stone keeps time, he says.
Hall's shut. Cantor Dorran walks the ridge road every morning to 'listen to the heather'.
He'll be back once somebody's made enough noise up there to bring him down. That's how it usually goes.
